entries.original_title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
entries.original_authors: Goetz, JG; Minguet, S; Navarro-Lérida, I; Lazcano, JJ; Samaniego, R; Calvo, E; Tello, M; Osteso-Ibáñez, T; Pellinen, T; Echarri, A; Cerezo, A; Klein-Szanto, AJ; Garcia, R; Keely, PJ; Sánchez-Mateos, P; Cukierman, E; Del Pozo, MA
entries.description: The original study claimed that Cav1WT primary mouse embryonic fibroblasts have greater extracellular-matrix remodeling and collagen contraction capabilities than Cav1KO fibroblasts; the replication tested this with a collagen gel contraction assay.
entries.citation_sentence: Although the data were not reported, the original study stated that the ECM remodeling capabilities of Cav1KO pMEFs were reduced compared to Cav1WT pMEFs, similar to the results reported with immortalized MEFs (Goetz et al., 2011).
entries.notes: The replication found reduced contraction in Cav1KO pMEFs, in the same direction as the original claim.

entries.original_title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
entries.original_authors: Goetz, JG; Minguet, S; Navarro-Lérida, I; Lazcano, JJ; Samaniego, R; Calvo, E; Tello, M; Osteso-Ibáñez, T; Pellinen, T; Echarri, A; Cerezo, A; Klein-Szanto, AJ; Garcia, R; Keely, PJ; Sánchez-Mateos, P; Cukierman, E; Del Pozo, MA
entries.description: The original study reported that stromal Cav1 status does not substantially alter primary tumor growth in mice injected with LM-4175 cells with or without Cav1WT or Cav1KO pMEFs; the replication tested this primary tumor growth outcome.
entries.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 7C and Supplemental Figure 7C of Goetz et al. (2011) and described in Protocols 3 and 4 in the Registered Report (Fiering et al., 2015).
entries.notes: The replication found no statistically significant difference in primary tumor growth and interpreted this as suggesting that primary tumor growth does not change when Cav1 is absent from the tumor stroma.

entries.original_title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
entries.original_authors: Goetz, JG; Minguet, S; Navarro-Lérida, I; Lazcano, JJ; Samaniego, R; Calvo, E; Tello, M; Osteso-Ibáñez, T; Pellinen, T; Echarri, A; Cerezo, A; Klein-Szanto, AJ; Garcia, R; Keely, PJ; Sánchez-Mateos, P; Cukierman, E; Del Pozo, MA
entries.description: The original study claimed that Cav1-positive tumor stroma increases metastatic burden compared with Cav1KO stroma or tumor cells without stromal fibroblasts; the replication tested metastatic foci formation in the corresponding mouse groups.
entries.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 7C and Supplemental Figure 7C of Goetz et al. (2011) and described in Protocols 3 and 4 in the Registered Report (Fiering et al., 2015).
entries.notes: The replication authors reported that metastatic results were not in the same direction as the original study and were not statistically significant.

entries.original_title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
entries.original_authors: Goetz, JG; Minguet, S; Navarro-Lérida, I; Lazcano, JJ; Samaniego, R; Calvo, E; Tello, M; Osteso-Ibáñez, T; Pellinen, T; Echarri, A; Cerezo, A; Klein-Szanto, AJ; Garcia, R; Keely, PJ; Sánchez-Mateos, P; Cukierman, E; Del Pozo, MA
entries.description: The original study claimed that co-injection with Cav1WT fibroblasts increases intratumoral fibronectin fiber alignment relative to tumor cells alone or Cav1KO fibroblasts; the replication measured fibronectin fiber orientation in primary tumors.
entries.citation_sentence: This compares to the original study that reported a statistically significant increase in fibronectin fiber alignment when LM-4175 cells were co-injected with Cav1WT pMEFs [Mdn = 52.5%, IQR = 43.6–55.4%, n = 8] compared to LM-4175 cells [Mdn = 36.9%, IQR = 36.8–37.7%, n = 5] or LM-4175 plus Cav1KO pMEFs [Mdn = 42.2%, IQR = 40.8–43.2%, n = 10], suggesting stromal Cav1 remodels the intratumoral microenvironment (Goetz et al., 2011).
entries.notes: The replication effect was in the same direction but not statistically significant, and the analysis workflow differed from the original.

entries.original_title: Biomechanical remodeling of the microenvironment by stromal caveolin-1 favors tumor invasion and metastasis
entries.original_authors: Goetz, JG; Minguet, S; Navarro-Lérida, I; Lazcano, JJ; Samaniego, R; Calvo, E; Tello, M; Osteso-Ibáñez, T; Pellinen, T; Echarri, A; Cerezo, A; Klein-Szanto, AJ; Garcia, R; Keely, PJ; Sánchez-Mateos, P; Cukierman, E; Del Pozo, MA
entries.description: The original study claimed a positive relationship between intratumoral fibronectin fiber alignment and metastatic burden; the replication tested the correlation between fibronectin fiber orientation and total metastatic foci.
entries.citation_sentence: The same type of analysis was reported in the original study, which indicated a statistically significant positive relationship (Goetz et al., 2011).
entries.notes: The replication found a statistically significant relationship in the opposite direction and explicitly summarized the result as opposite to the original study.
